content.value_statement: Live meetings move quickly, and teams need current context without searching across tools. This skill helps an assistant join Lark meetings, read event timelines, and leave when work is complete.
actual_capabilities: Join an in-progress Lark video meeting by a 9-digit meeting number.
Leave a meeting by the long meeting ID returned from join or search.
Read live meeting events, including participants, chats, transcripts, and screen sharing activity.
Use pagination controls to retrieve complete visible event timelines.
Preview join, leave, and event requests through lark-cli dry-run options.
Route finished-meeting requests to the separate Lark video meeting skills.
limitations: Requires an authenticated Lark user session and the lark-cli binary.
Only works for meetings the bot can join or has recently attended.
Cannot replace post-meeting minutes, recordings, or participant snapshot tools.
Meeting actions are visible to other participants and may create audit records.

use_cases.title: Attend Active Meetings
use_cases.description: Join an in-progress meeting for a user and keep the returned meeting ID for later actions.

use_cases.title: Track Live Meeting Events
use_cases.description: Read the current event timeline to understand speakers, chats, joins, leaves, and shared content.

use_cases.title: Close Bot Participation
use_cases.description: Leave a meeting when monitoring is complete and route post-meeting work to the correct Lark skill.

prompt_templates.title: Join a Meeting
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for a visible bot join action.
prompt_templates.prompt: Join Lark meeting 123456789 as the meeting assistant, confirm the visible action before running it, and save the returned meeting ID.

prompt_templates.title: Check Current Events
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate request after the bot has joined.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the saved meeting ID to get the latest visible Lark meeting events with full pagination, then summarize speakers, chats, and shares.

prompt_templates.title: Monitor New Activity
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced request for repeated live updates.
prompt_templates.prompt: Continue from the saved page token, fetch new Lark meeting events, report changes since the last check, and keep the new token.

prompt_templates.title: Complete Meeting Handoff
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced workflow across live and post-meeting tasks.
prompt_templates.prompt: Leave the current meeting with the saved meeting ID, then route any minutes or transcript request to the appropriate Lark video meeting skill.

output_examples.output: The bot joined the active meeting and recorded the long meeting ID for later event checks or leaving.

output_examples.input: What changed since the last event check?
output: Two participants joined after the saved cursor.
A new chat message was received.
No active screen share was reported.

output_examples.output: The bot left the meeting by using the saved meeting ID. Other participants can see that the bot has left.

best_practices: Confirm the meeting number source before joining, because the bot becomes visible to participants.
Store the returned meeting ID and page token for leave and incremental event checks.
Use the separate post-meeting skills for recordings, minutes, and historical participant snapshots.
anti_patterns: Do not join meetings only to fetch historical data.
Do not reuse old event results when the user asks for current meeting status.
Do not pass a 9-digit meeting number where a long meeting ID is required.

faq.question: What does this skill do?
faq.answer: It helps an assistant join active Lark meetings, read live meeting events, and leave meetings when finished.

faq.question: Does the bot join meetings invisibly?
faq.answer: No. The bot appears in the participant list, and the meeting may record its participation.

faq.question: Can it read past meetings?
faq.answer: No. Use the related Lark video meeting skills for historical meetings, recordings, minutes, and participant snapshots.

faq.question: Which identifier should I provide?
faq.answer: Use a 9-digit meeting number to join. Use the long meeting ID for events and leave actions.

faq.question: Does it require authentication?
faq.answer: Yes. It requires lark-cli, a logged-in user session, and the Lark scopes for the requested operation.

faq.question: When should I leave the meeting?
faq.answer: Leave after the monitoring task is complete or when the user asks the bot to stop participating.
